description: ECC + specific curves decomposed. Mathematical foundation (elliptic curve over finite field). Discrete logarithm problem. NIST curves (P-256, P-384, P-521). Curve25519 + Ed25519. secp256k1 (Bitcoin). The implementation gotchas (constant-time, side channels, signature malleability).

sub_mechanisms.name: elliptic_curve_equation
sub_mechanisms.definition: y² = x³ + ax + b mod p. Points on curve form group under specific addition rule.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation. Group operation = elliptic curve addition. Repeated addition = scalar multiplication. Discrete log of scalar multiplication is hard.

sub_mechanisms.name: ECDLP_discrete_log_problem
sub_mechanisms.definition: Given P, Q = kP, find k. Hard for well-chosen curves.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of ECC security. 256-bit ECC ≈ 3072-bit RSA security. Shor's algorithm breaks (motivating post-quantum migration).

sub_mechanisms.name: scalar_multiplication
sub_mechanisms.definition: kP = P + P + ... + P (k times). Computed via double-and-add in log(k) steps.
sub_mechanisms.why: Core ECC operation. Must be constant-time to avoid side channels. Modern: Montgomery ladder, scalar masking.

sub_mechanisms.name: NIST_P256
sub_mechanisms.definition: secp256r1. NIST-standardised curve. 128-bit security. Widely deployed.
sub_mechanisms.why: TLS, FIDO2, many protocols default. Concerns: NSA involvement in parameter selection. Used heavily despite community preference for Curve25519.

sub_mechanisms.name: Curve25519_design
sub_mechanisms.definition: Bernstein 2005. Twisted Edwards curve. y² + x² = 1 + dx²y² mod 2^255 - 19.
sub_mechanisms.why: Modern default for new protocols. Designed to be safer to implement: constant-time scalar mult straightforward, no special-case handling.

sub_mechanisms.name: Ed25519_signatures
sub_mechanisms.definition: Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm on Curve25519. Deterministic signatures (no per-signature randomness).
sub_mechanisms.why: Standard in SSH, GitHub commits, Signal. Fast (~70K sig/s/core). Deterministic: same message → same signature (catches RNG failure that breaks ECDSA).

sub_mechanisms.name: ECDSA_signatures
sub_mechanisms.definition: Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm. Requires fresh random per signature.
sub_mechanisms.why: FIPS-compliant. Bitcoin (secp256k1), TLS, most protocols. CRITICAL: nonce reuse leaks private key (PS3 hack). Modern code uses RFC 6979 deterministic ECDSA.

sub_mechanisms.name: secp256k1_Bitcoin
sub_mechanisms.definition: Koblitz curve. y² = x³ + 7. Chosen for Bitcoin by Satoshi.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of Bitcoin + Ethereum + most cryptocurrencies. Different curve than NIST P-256. Implementations (libsecp256k1) heavily optimised + audited.

sub_mechanisms.name: constant_time_implementation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Operations run in time independent of secret values. No data-dependent branches or memory accesses.
sub_mechanisms.why: Timing side channels reveal secrets. Modern ECC libraries are constant-time. Older or naive implementations leak via timing. Critical for security.

sub_mechanisms.name: ECDH_key_exchange
sub_mechanisms.definition: Each party generates ephemeral key pair, exchanges public keys, computes shared secret = privA * pubB = privB * pubA.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of TLS 1.3, Signal, WireGuard. With ephemeral keys (ECDHE) provides forward secrecy. Standard for modern key agreement.

sub_mechanisms.name: signature_malleability
sub_mechanisms.definition: Same message + private key may produce different valid signatures (e.g., negating s in ECDSA).
sub_mechanisms.why: Issue for systems that rely on signature uniqueness (Bitcoin's transaction IDs). Mitigation: canonical signature form. Ed25519 is malleability-free by design.

sub_mechanisms.name: post_quantum_threat_to_ECC
sub_mechanisms.definition: Shor's algorithm on sufficiently large quantum computer breaks ECDLP. ECC needs migration to PQ.
sub_mechanisms.why: Same threat as RSA. Hybrid schemes (ECDH + Kyber) provide transition. Long-term secrets must migrate now (harvest-now-decrypt-later).

derivation_rules.name: ECC_security_per_bit_higher_than_RSA
derivation_rules.why: ECDLP is harder per bit than factoring. Smaller keys + faster operations. Modern protocols favor ECC.

derivation_rules.name: Curve25519_designed_for_safer_implementation
then: Curve25519 has fewer edge cases than NIST curves
derivation_rules.why: No special-case point handling, natural constant-time form, no co-factor concerns. Bernstein designed for implementer safety. Standard choice for new protocols.

derivation_rules.name: ECDSA_nonce_reuse_leaks_private_key
if: two ECDSA signatures use the same nonce
then: private key recoverable from the two signatures
derivation_rules.why: PS3 ECDSA hack: Sony reused nonce. Mathematical fact: 2 equations in 2 unknowns (k, privkey). RFC 6979 deterministic ECDSA derives nonce from message + key, preventing failure.

derivation_rules.name: Ed25519_deterministic_signatures
then: same key + message → same signature, no randomness needed
derivation_rules.why: Nonce derived deterministically from key + message. No RNG failure mode. Same signature is verification-friendly. Modern preferred over ECDSA when possible.

derivation_rules.name: ECDH_with_ephemeral_keys_provides_forward_secrecy
if: each session uses fresh ephemeral keys
then: compromise of long-term keys doesn't expose past sessions
derivation_rules.why: Session keys derived from ephemeral DH; discarded after use. Stolen long-term key tomorrow can't decrypt today's traffic. Required property in modern protocols.
